rule: Ground feathers ward lanterns from wraiths
texts: When a Keeper grinds feathers and scatters the feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers ward the lantern against wraiths.
Whenever a Keeper grinds feathers and spreads the feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers shield the lantern against wraiths.
Wraiths do not approach a warded lantern.
Stale ground feathers do not ward lanterns.

fields.sentence: When a Keeper grinds feathers and scatters the feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers ward the lantern against wraiths.
parse: (: whenever_grind_scatter_ward (Implication (And (Member $k keeper) (GroupOf $f feather) (Member $n lantern) (Member $n lit) (Member $g grind) (Agent $g $k) (Patient $g $f) (Member $s scatter) (Agent $s $k) (Theme $s $f) (Around $s $n)) (And (Member (sk_ward $f $n) ward) (Agent (sk_ward $f $n) $f) (Theme (sk_ward $f $n) $n) (Against (sk_ward $f $n) wraith) (During (sk_ward $f $n) $s))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q2_gaps: a "when P, Q" trigger built from TWO coordinated events (grinds ... and scatters ...): the whenever template assumes one trigger occurrence, and the instruction set does not say which event the per-occurrence Skolem consequent is a function of, nor which one the During link attaches to
review.notes: The consequent Skolem (sk_ward $f $n) is keyed on the two participants instead of on a trigger occurrence, so two scatterings of the same feathers around the same lantern would collapse into one warding event — the composition the gap above leaves undecided. Patient for grinding, Theme for scattering and for the warded lantern, the Around/Against surface-preposition obliques, the lit modifier kept in participle form, and 1.0/0.9 all follow the instruction set.

fields.sentence: Whenever a Keeper grinds feathers and spreads the feathers around a lit lantern, the feathers shield the lantern against wraiths.
parse: (: keeper_shield_rule (Implication (And (Member $k keeper) (Member $g grind) (Agent $g $k) (Patient $g $f) (GroupOf $f feather) (Member $s spread) (Agent $s $k) (Theme $s $f) (Around $s $l) (Member $l lantern) (Member $l lit)) (And (Member (sk_shield $k $f $l) shield) (Agent (sk_shield $k $f $l) $f) (Theme (sk_shield $k $f $l) $l) (Against (sk_shield $k $f $l) wraith) (During (sk_shield $k $f $l) $s))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: The whenever machinery is applied correctly: plain-variable premises for the two coordinated trigger clauses, a per-occurrence Skolem-function consequent, the During tie to the trigger, no QuantifierPhrase companion, and coreference of 'the feathers'/'the lantern' back to the premise variables. Two defensible judgment calls: Theme for 'spreads the feathers' (displacement, not change) and the surface oblique Around rather than Location for the spread's PP.

fields.sentence: Wraiths do not approach a warded lantern.

q2_gaps: an indefinite singular OBJECT inside a negated verbal generic ("Ns do not V a warded N"): the instruction set does not say whether it becomes a second universal premise (the parse's forall-not reading) or a witness inside the strength-0 bundle — "Negation does not re-decide the subject" speaks only to the subject, the Coopers/barrel example uses a definite object, and the two-universal Skolem-function machinery is licensed only for explicit universals
review.notes: Strength-0 distributing rule at (STV 0.0 0.9) matches the negated-verbal-generic pattern exactly, with no QuantifierPhrase (plain "not" takes none); "warded" correctly stays a participial adjective split from the head rather than a fused kind. The forall-not rendering of the indefinite object is the semantically right reading even though no rule licenses it.

parse: (: fresh_ground_feather_ward_rule (Implication (And (Member $x feather) (Member $x fresh) (Member $x ground)) (And (Member (sk_ward $x) ward) (Agent (sk_ward $x) $x) (Theme (sk_ward $x) lantern))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

review.notes: The adjectivally-restricted kind subject correctly forces the distributing-rule route instead of a kind-level relation, with the restrictions as premise conjuncts and the participial modifier kept in its surface form "ground". Bare-generic (STV 0.9 0.9) with no QuantifierPhrase companion and Agent for the inanimate transitive subject are both right.

fields.sentence: Stale ground feathers do not ward lanterns.
parse: (: feathers_no_ward (Implication (And (Member $x feather) (Member $x stale) (Member $x ground)) (And (Member (sk_ward $x) ward) (Agent (sk_ward $x) $x) (Theme (sk_ward $x) lantern))) (STV 0.0 0.9))

review.notes: The parse reads 'ground' as a participial modifier, which is what licenses the separate (Member $x ground) premise; on the competing noun-modifier reading it would instead have to fuse as ground_feather with a genus atom and no exposed modifier. Everything else - the strength-0.0 distributing rule for the restricted bare-plural kind subject, and Theme for the unchanged object - matches the instruction set.
